stem: In the figure, points \(P\), \(O\), and \(Q\) lie on a line. What is the value of \(x\)?
solution: Angles \(QOR\) and \(ROP\) together form the straight angle \(QOP\), so they add up to \(180^{\circ}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This assumes the two angles are equal. They form a straight line, so they add up to 180°.
explanation.B: Correct. Angles that form a straight line add up to 180°: \(x = 180 - 38 = 142\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is \(90 - 38\); the angles form a straight line (180°), not a right angle (90°).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is \(90 + 38\). The two angles together make 180°, so subtract 38 from 180.

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'A': 'A', 'D': 'B', 'B': 'C', 'C': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'A', 'B': 'D', 'C': 'B', 'D': 'C'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert P['P'][1]==P['O'][1]==P['Q'][1]
assert abs(ang('Q','O','R')-38)<0.1
ans=180-38
assert abs(ang('R','O','P')-ans)<0.1
assert value(choices[answer])==ans
assert all(value(choices[k])!=ans for k in choices if k!=answer)
